subject: science
notes: Mangroves are trees that grow in salty coastal water; their tangled roots trap mud and shelter young fish.
Large areas of mangrove forest near Karachi, Pakistan, have been lost to cutting and to reduced freshwater flow from the Indus River.
Marine ecologist Samina Baloch wanted to find out whether replanted mangroves shelter as many young fish as natural stands do.
Over two years, her team netted fish at 10 replanted sites and 10 natural sites along the Karachi coast.
Replanted sites that were more than five years old sheltered about as many young fish as natural sites, while younger replanted sites sheltered far fewer.
stem: The student wants to present the aim and the finding of Baloch's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Because large areas of mangrove forest near Karachi have been lost to cutting and reduced river flow, Baloch studied replanted mangroves along the coast.
choices.B: Baloch found that replanted mangrove sites more than five years old sheltered about as many young fish as natural sites, while younger replanted sites sheltered far fewer.
choices.C: Baloch's team netted fish over two years at 10 replanted mangrove sites and 10 natural sites along the coast near Karachi, Pakistan.
choices.D: Testing whether replanted mangroves shelter as many young fish as natural stands, Baloch found that only replanted sites more than five years old matched the natural ones.

explanation.why: The goal has two parts: the aim (what Baloch wanted to find out) and the finding (what she learned). The key must include both the question about replanted mangroves and young fish and the result that only older replanted sites matched natural ones.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This gives the background to the study and hints at its subject, but it states neither the precise aim nor any finding.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This states the finding fully but never says what the study set out to test.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This describes the method, how the fish were counted, and gives neither the aim nor the finding.
explanation.D: Correct. "Testing whether" gives the aim, and "found that" gives the finding.
